title: Mid-sprint kernel coalesce briefing - week of 2027-05-03
content:
Purpose:
A compact mid-sprint sync capturing outcomes from the kernel-prefetch/coalesce experiments, KV-cache shadowing runs, and new batching heuristics tests. Intended for the serving-runtime team and cross-team stakeholders (SRE, infra, and product).

TL;DR:
- Coalescer tuning (alpha) reduces p50 token latency on short queries (~8–10 tokens) by ~7.5% in lab runs; p95 unchanged.
- KV shadow cache ran at 80% coverage for tail traffic; observed ~12% fewer repeated KV lookups per session but introduced a hiccup in small-batch throughput on A100 hosts.
- New adaptive-batch cutoff prototype reduces CPU spin on cold paths; needs additional telemetry before we promote.

Wins / Positive signals:
- Kernel patch r1482 (fast-prefetch-path) merged to feature branch; microbenchmarks show 9–11% improvement in single-token generate step for our compact transformer variant.
- Coalescer config v3 (shard-delay=2ms, max-coalesce=24) gave the best tradeoff for regional EU workloads during simulated bursts.
- Two flaky test cases from earlier runs (kv-dedup-check) were fixed by using deterministic eviction order in the shadow cache.

Data snapshot (lab vs staging):
- baseline lab (no coalesce changes): p50 token latency 11.9ms, p95 token latency 38.2ms, throughput 4.8k tok/s
- coalesce v3 lab: p50 11.0ms, p95 37.9ms, throughput 4.7k tok/s
- staging KV-shadow 80% coverage: repeat-lookup-rate down 12% (from 0.42 to 0.37 lookups/session), CPU tail on A100 up ~4% under small-batch load
Note: numbers are synthetic runs against demo models; production sampling still pending.

Experiments run this week (short notes):
1) Coalescer sweep (v1..v5): latency and fairness matrix across sequence lengths. Observed that higher max-coalesce helps long sequences but harms short-latency tail; v3 is best midpoint.
2) KV-shadow tuning: changed eviction window logic to be time-aware (instead of only count-based). Reduced unnecessary evictions for persistent sessions.
3) Adaptive-batch cutoff: prototype that lowers batching window for requests with predicted short-token lengths (using a tiny length-predictor model). Cut spin but introduced some oscillation under sudden traffic spike.
4) Kernel fast-path micro-optimizations: hoisted few memcpy ops and avoided a redundant range check in attention kernel.

Observations / Anomalies:
- One reproducible regression: when coalescer delay < 1ms and max-coalesce >= 48, we see queue-starvation on hosts with fewer concurrent streams. Likely scheduling fairness bug in the runtime's queue head. Adding a deterministic jitter solved it in lab.
- KV-shadow integration in the allocator: under low memory headroom, shadow entries were evicted aggressively and then reinserted frequently, causing thrash. Proposal: add a soft cap that reduces shadow writes when free memory < threshold.
- Batch-cutoff predictor false positives: for long-seq requests predicted as short, we hurt throughput. Need to add confidence gating and a fallback.

Standup highlights (bulleted, fast):
- Leah: validated coalescer v3 in EU staging traffic replay; wants canary next week (2% traffic).
- Omar: kernel patch landed on feature branch; working on CI perf regression guard.
- Priya: KV-shadow rollout script updated; wants approval to flip shadow on dedicated infra for an hour.
- Ethan: collecting end-to-end traces from prod-sim runs; will share waterfall screenshots in #serving-runtime.

Decisions made:
- Promote coalescer v3 to canary for EU region (2% traffic) next Tuesday morning. Rollback plan: disable coalescer via runtime flags and revert to v2 within 30 minutes if error rate or p95 regressions > 5%.
- Hold adaptive-batch cutoff until we have confidence gating and three more synthetic spike tests.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Leah: prepare canary rollout doc + telemetry dashboard tiles (ETA: 2027-05-09)
- Omar: add perf-guard CI job benchmark for kernel fast-path (ETA: 2027-05-07)
- Priya: implement soft-cap in KV-shadow write path to avoid thrash (ETA: 2027-05-10)
- Ethan: run end-to-end prod-sim with coalescer v3 at 2% traffic and post traces (ETA: 2027-05-09)
- Martin (owner): coordinate cross-team rollback drill and write short runbook (ETA: 2027-05-11)

Blockers / Risks:
- Telemetry gap: we don't have per-model cache-hit attribution in current dashboards; need a taggable KV key in tracing. Without it, root-cause during canary could be slow.
- Infra constraint: A100 fleet small-batch CPU increase may affect other tenant workloads; need SRE signoff for canary window.

Notes-to-self / loose ideas (informal):
- Try a tiny leaky-bucket on coalescer admission instead of fixed delay; might stabilize under bursty arrivals.
- Instrument per-kernel memory watermark to detect pre-spill thrash earlier.
- Capture a short video of waterfall traces to share with the product team — they understand visual latency impact better than numbers.

Meeting follow-ups / links:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1482 (fast-prefetch-path, bench numbers in description)
- Linear: INF-8762 (KV prefetch coalesce experiment)
- Runbook template: confluence:SERVING/CANARY-ROLLBACK-TEMPLATE (placeholder link in doc)

Appendix (quick checklist for canary):
- [ ] Dashboard ready (p50/p95, error-rate, kv-hit-rate, cpu by host)
- [ ] Rollout automation test pass
- [ ] SRE notified and on-call scheduled for window
- [ ] Nightly backup snapshot created for the canary routing group

If you see anything missing or want a deeper dive into any of the experiment logs, ping me directly or add to this doc.

-- Martin
